messages.text: Verstappen, Lawson receive grid penalties after 'unacceptable' practice collision

metadata.summary: Max Verstappen and Liam Lawson have both received one-grid place penalties for an "unacceptable" collision in second practice at the Mexico City Grand Prix.
metadata.content: Max Verstappen, Liam Lawson receive grid penalties for 'unacceptable' practice collision at Mexico City Grand Prix | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Breaking Max Verstappen, Liam Lawson receive grid penalties for 'unacceptable' practice collision at Mexico City Grand Prix Max Verstappen and Liam Lawson have both been handed a one-place grid penalty for their collision in second practice at the Mexico City Grand Prix; watch qualifying in Mexico at 9pm on Saturday and the race at 8pm on Sunday Saturday 31 October 2026 03:12, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson and Red Bull's Max Verstappen make contact during FP2 at the Mexico City GP Max Verstappen and Liam Lawson have both received one-grid place penalties for an "unacceptable" collision in second practice at the Mexico City Grand Prix. Verstappen tried to overtake Lawson up the inside at Turn 12 going into the old baseball stadium but the Racing Bulls driver held his ground, so the pair went side by side through Turn 13 and made contact at Turn 14 with a piece of debris falling off the Dutchman's car and causing a red flag. Collisions of this nature between drivers in practice are extremely rare, and the stewards stated both drivers "behaved in a manner that was considered unacceptable" and that a warning had been given at the team managers meeting earlier on Friday about overtaking in the final sector. messages.text: Leclerc seals Mexico City practice double as Hamilton suffers technical issue

metadata.summary: Charles Leclerc completed a Friday practice double at the Mexico City Grand Prix but Ferrari's strong showing was dampened by Lewis Hamilton suffering a technical issue.
metadata.content: Mexico City GP: Charles Leclerc completes Friday practice double as Ferrari team-mate Lewis Hamilton suffers technical failure | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Mexico City GP: Charles Leclerc completes Friday practice double as Ferrari team-mate Lewis Hamilton suffers technical failure Charles Leclerc tops both Friday practice sessions for Ferrari; Lewis Hamilton suffers technical failure; Max Verstappen collides with Liam Lawson; watch every Mexico City GP session live on Sky Sports F1, with qualifying at 9pm on Saturday and the race at 8pm on Sunday Saturday 31 October 2026 03:14, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from Friday's practice sessions at the Mexico City Grand Prix Charles Leclerc completed a Friday practice double at the Mexico City Grand Prix but Ferrari's strong showing was dampened by Lewis Hamilton suffering a technical issue. Leclerc produced a time of 1:17.827s to finish just over a tenth clear of McLaren's Lando Norris and Mercedes' George Russell, with the British pair among 10 drivers who had earlier sat out the opening session to make way for rookie drivers. Kimi Antonelli, who only needs to finish ninth in Sunday's race to become Formula 1's youngest-ever world champion, was a tenth down on his team-mate Russell in fourth. messages.text: How Antonelli can win world title at Mexico City GP on Sunday

metadata.summary: Kimi Antonelli was unable to seal the Formula 1 world championship at the first race where it was mathematically possible for him to do so, but the Italian has left himself with a great opportunity to make history this weekend in Mexico City.
metadata.content: Kimi Antonelli F1 title permutations: How Mercedes driver can win 2026 Formula 1 Drivers' Championship at Mexico City GP on Sunday | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Kimi Antonelli F1 title permutations: How Mercedes driver can win 2026 Formula 1 Drivers' Championship at Mexico City GP on Sunday How can Kimi Antonelli become the youngest champion in Formula 1 history this Sunday at the Mexico City Grand Prix? Watch every session of the Mexico City GP from this Friday, live on Sky Sports F1 Saturday 31 October 2026 02:23, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli looks ahead to Mexico as he moves to brink of a title win Kimi Antonelli was unable to seal the Formula 1 world championship at the first race where it was mathematically possible for him to do so, but the Italian has left himself with a great opportunity to make history this weekend in Mexico City. Antonelli won the United States Grand Prix in Austin to move 123 points clear of his Mercedes team-mate and nearest challenger George Russell, and 124 points ahead of Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton. Red Bull's Max Verstappen, Ferrari's Charles Leclerc and McLaren's Lando Norris were officially knocked out of championship contention, leaving Russell and Hamilton as the only drivers who can technically prevent Antonelli from becoming the sport's youngest ever world champion at 20 years old. messages.text: Brilliant Sun Goddess in class of her own at Breeders' Cup

metadata.summary: Sun Goddess confirmed herself as a two-year-old out of the ordinary with a clear-cut win Breeders' Cup Juvenile Fillies Turf at Keeneland.
metadata.content: Breeders' Cup: Sun Goddess in class of her own with Juvenile Fillies Turf win at Keeneland as Libertango takes Juvenile Turf Sprint | Racing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Breeders' Cup: Sun Goddess in class of her own with Juvenile Fillies Turf win at Keeneland as Libertango takes Juvenile Turf Sprint Sun Goddess capped off a memorable two-year-old season with a fourth success at the top level with a scintillating display in the Breeders' Cup Juvenile Fillies Turf on a winning night for the European raiders at Keeneland; Libertango won the opening Juvenile Turf Sprint Friday 30 October 2026 22:08, UK Image: Sun Goddess, ridden by Ryan Moore, wins the John Deere Breeders' Cup Juvenile Fillies Turf at Keeneland Sun Goddess confirmed herself as a two-year-old out of the ordinary with a clear-cut win Breeders' Cup Juvenile Fillies Turf at Keeneland. Seen by many as the banker of the two-day meeting, she already had three Group Ones in Europe to her credit but she had to contend with the journey to America and stall nine. However, Ryan Moore got her out of the stalls sharply and across to the inside in the perfect position just behind the leader whereas her main market rival, Francis-Henri Graffard's Amusingly, had to settle at the rear of the field. As soon as Moore kicked clear early in the straight the race was over as a contest and once again it was left to Joseph O'Brien's Green Empress to chase her home, the fourth time she has been second to the winner this year.
